schema.headline: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
schema.name: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
schema.description: An order automorphism of a Dlab group resists ambient conjugation after every embedding, with unrestricted slopes and precise endpoint conditions.
schema.abstract: Let G=D⟨2⟩([0,1]) be the compactly supported, locally right 2^ℤ-affine Dlab group. We construct an automorphism preserving both Dlab orders and give a proof that it cannot be implemented after any embedding in either of two explicitly defined groups: all locally right affine increasing interval homeomorphisms, and all locally right affine increasing real homeomorphisms that are affine on an initial ray. The ambient slopes are unrestricted, and the embedding need not preserve an order. Perfectness separates the supports of commuting local groups; a two-tail construction handles both possible orientations of their least action components. This extends a one-tail mechanism used in prior work. The definitions and affine-germ decomposition of the standard Dlab families place them in these ambient groups. Consequently the construction gives an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Problem 21.149, including arbitrary positive-real slope groups and the full and reflected extended-real families.
